evidence.quote: Concept explanations, conceptual hints, test-design discussion without executable test code, and administrative/logistics questions are allowed throughout the course.
Debugging assistance is allowed only after the student supplies a concrete attempt, observation, failing test, or error message.
For graded work, AI may not produce implementation code, pseudocode algorithms for the assigned solution, executable tests, a complete solution, or submission-ready written explanations.
For a1 only, executable unit or integration tests may be generated by AI.
Debugging requires a concrete attempt or observed failure.
AI-generated implementation code, solution pseudocode, complete solutions, and submission-ready writeups remain prohibited.
with no permission to generate executable tests.
AI-generated test code, solution pseudocode, implementation code, whole solutions, and submission-ready rationales are prohibited.
AI can explain allocation concepts and discuss categories of edge cases without producing runnable tests.
Debugging the student's own test requires the student's actual attempt or an observed failure.
For a3, AI-generated implementation code, solution pseudocode, executable tests, and test-design discussion are permitted.
Concepts, hints, logistics, and evidence-based debugging are permitted.
Debugging still requires an attempt or observed error.
A complete submission including the written analysis, or any submission-ready analysis/writeup, is prohibited.

Students may request conceptual explanations, hints, debugging, test-design discussion, executable tests, pseudocode, implementation code, complete worked solutions, written explanations, and logistics.
No prior attempt is required here, including for debugging.
